providers_note: ib joined mlx5dv on 2026-09-09 and is required for a self-consistent capture, not for extra coverage. NVSHMEM's ibdevx transport creates its queue pairs with plain verbs; ibv_destroy_qp is interposed by the engine so the closes are always recorded, while ibv_create_qp is interposed by the ibverbs provider, so a mlx5dv-only run recorded 99 closes per rank naming entities nothing had opened. Measured, same workload and node (job 45636769): -p mlx5dv gives ib_queue_pair 0 rows and 99 orphans per rank, -p ib,mlx5dv gives 198 rows and 0 orphans, with the 200-range streams identical across both.
topology: 1 node x2 A100 PEs over one ConnectX-5, NVSHMEM put-ring forced through the NIC with P2P disabled, CPU-driven DEVX (ibdevx), NIC buffers registered through nvidia_peermem
golden: none, by design — same reasoning as cases 09 and 10
why: SigmaTrace's published artifact configuration, and the third corner of a deliberate design. Cases 09, 10 and 11 differ from one another by exactly one variable each: 09→10 changes the umem binding, 10→11 changes the transport. Read together they separate what the provider decodes from who drives the hardware.
why_not_device_initiated: ibdevx drives the DEVX control plane from the CPU. There is no GPU-initiated data plane here and none is asserted — ibgda_engaged is deliberately ABSENT rather than expect_fail, because asserting device-initiated traffic in a CPU-driven transport would be asserting a bug rather than recording one. What this case proves is that the DEVX decoding, the umem registry and topology closure hold independently of who rings the doorbell, which cases 09 and 10 structurally cannot show because there the two always move together.
prerequisite_note: requires nvidia_peermem but NOT PeerMappingOverride=1, unlike cases 09 and 10. PeerMappingOverride exists to let the NIC's UAR doorbell page be mapped into the GPU's address space, which is what a GPU-initiated transport needs; ibdevx rings the doorbell from the CPU. Registering GPU buffers with the NIC by address still needs peermem. This narrower condition is intentional: if PeerMappingOverride turns out to be required after all, this case FAILS on a host that has peermem without it, rather than skipping and hiding the fact. A skip condition that is too broad makes a case invisible exactly where it would have been informative.
prerequisite_answer: THE EXPERIMENT ABOVE HAS RUN ON BOTH HOSTS, and PeerMappingOverride is NOT required — the narrow prerequisite stands exactly as written. Getting here took two wrong turns worth recording, because both were confident and neither was measured. Job 45636332 was the first time this case ever reached its assertions (it had been short-circuiting at the mpirun gate, and at the peermem gate before that). It ran on MN5's as01r1b32 — peermem loaded, PeerMappingOverride absent — and umem_binding_as_configured failed with 436 umems all at device=65535. That was read as the answer the note above was waiting for, and a PeerMappingOverride skip gate was added on 2026-09-10. It was wrong. du04 HAS PeerMappingOverride=1 and failed the same assertion identically (2026-09-11, 20 umems, all device=65535), so the driver flag was never the discriminator and the gate was reverted. What the du04 capture showed once the ibverbs provider was co-loaded: the umems are the DEVX control plane — 64 KiB work-queue rings and 8 B doorbell records, host-resident because the CPU writes them — while the NVSHMEM symmetric heap reached the NIC as a 512 MiB ib_mem_region at 0x620000000, which mem_owner resolved to device 0 on rank 0 and device 1 on rank 1. The transport DID hand GPU memory to the NIC. The assertion was scoped to mlx5_umem and could not see it. Fixed by declaring workload.umem_control_plane_only=1 (see the note on it), not by skipping the case or marking the assertion xfail — both of which were tried first and both of which would have buried a real finding under a false explanation.
comparison_note: this is the one configuration where SigmaTrace's results and comshu's can be compared directly. RAN 2026-09-14 on du04 (parity/README.md; two runs of each tool, both self-repeatable). Where both tools record a class they agree event for event — devices, memory regions, umems, UARs, DEVX connections — except ibv_dereg_mr, which SigmaTrace interposes and never records. comshu additionally records the DEVX queue pairs, commands, CQs, SRQ and the GPU that owns the heap's MR, none of which SigmaTrace has an event for. Neither tool captured the data plane in this configuration: the CPU rings a UAR that neither tool's doorbell path watches. comshu now does, through the send-queue watcher this case runs with since 2026-09-15 (data_plane_note); SigmaTrace still does not.
data_plane_note: captured with `comshu run --watch-send-queues`: the watcher reads each DEVX queue's doorbell record and send queue from outside the path, touches no doorbell, and counts what it misses in mlx5_send_coverage. Asserted every run: each rank moved exactly elems x iters RDMA writes of elem_bytes (2,048 x 4 B, measured on du04 before it was asserted), every watched row is a fully decoded Window, and each rank's coverage row exists with published == decoded and nothing lapped or dropped. NVSHMEM's ibdevx queues are RC on both hosts (ibdevx creates no other kind). On MN5 the watcher also takes UCX's DEVX queues — 40 RC and 15 DCI per rank, MPI's, created with dbr_umem_valid clear because the kernel sets it (MN5 job 45888686: 60 watched, 0 refused) — which carry no puts and are watched and counted all the same. The case runs with NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=8192: at the default 1,024 the watcher has ~200 us of slack against a proxy posting at least ~5 WQEBBs per us, and its routine 100-335 us polling gaps lapped the ring whenever one landed on a burst (MN5 job 45893428, 1024 x 20: 1,562 / 2,009 lapped at 1,024, none at 8,192). Design and measurements: plans/PLAN-20260914-1750-the-ibdevx-data-plane-is-a-host-send-queue.
loopback_note: same as cases 09 and 10: both PEs sit behind one HCA, so src_lid == dest_lid on every connection and that is correct. The invariant that survives loopback is closure, not distinctness.
umem_control_plane_only_note: 1 because ibdevx drives the control plane from the CPU: every umem this case registers is a work queue or a doorbell record — 64 KiB rings and 8 B doorbells, host-resident by design — and the GPU memory reaches the NIC through ibv_reg_mr instead. Measured on du04 2026-09-11: 10 umems per rank at device=65535, and one 512 MiB ib_mem_region at 0x620000000 that mem_owner resolved to device 0 on rank 0 and device 1 on rank 1. Without this flag umem_binding_as_configured demands a GPU-resident UMEM and reports 'the transport did not hand the GPU to the NIC at all', which is false here. Cases 09/10/12 must NOT set it: there the claim is that the work queues themselves are GPU-resident, and accepting an MR instead would let a capture with host-resident queues pass on its data heap.
workload_note: `mpirun -np 2 ... putget 1024 2`, the same binary as cases 09/10/12/25 and the same putget.cu as 04/06/07 — held constant so the transport is the only thing that varies from case 10. The binary carries sm_80 and sm_90 and is named for putget.cu's content; until d45b536 it was sm_80 only, and on MN5's H100s its kernel never launched while the run still printed OK.
oracle_note: without ibgda_engaged this case has no transport-engagement guard of its own, and expect_tables is what stands in for one: a silent fallback to a non-DEVX transport (ibrc) produces no 200-range streams at all, which expect_tables turns into a red board rather than an empty pass. That substitution is worth stating because it is weaker than case 09's guard — it catches 'no DEVX at all', not 'DEVX but not the transport we asked for'. Since the data plane is captured, the exact-put assertion is the stronger guard it lacked: a transport that did not carry the workload's writes through these DEVX queues cannot produce elems x iters of them per rank.
